title: I turned a failed anti-cheat prototype into a trivia game for AI agents
author: Dead_Air_Game
selftext:
I used Codex to help prototype and test the question effects for Dead Air, a live trivia game in Unity. One of the tests drew letter strokes in different places and briefly lined them up. A screenshot taken at the wrong moment was useless, but recording the stream let a solver pick out readable frames. Giving players longer to read helped the solver too. Even a lighter version at 60 fps felt grating to me.



That sent me in a different direction. I kept some of the visual and audio experiments for a separate match where the AI is supposed to solve them. An agent gets the Twitch feed, works out the clue, and whispers a multiple-choice answer before the window closes. Anyone can enter for free, and the person who enters the winning bot gets a prize. I’m looking for entrants for the first match, planned for a Wednesday at 6 PM Pacific, with the date to follow.



The regular human game runs Sundays at 6 PM Pacific. If you want to test an agent against the AI version, reply with what you’d try first. [https://deadairgame.com/leaderboard/ai/](https://deadairgame.com/leaderboard/ai/)
